title: Payload types keyed by event name
summary: Constrain with keyof, break inference, then push into mapped and conditional types.

turns.user: kill every any in Emitter. i want on('save', p => p.id) to complete properly

assistant.body: Making on generic over keyof Events. K falls out of name, so the handler payload lands on Events[K]. The internal bag stays loose and only the public surface gets nailed down.
emit takes K as well. I am pulling the payload type out into its own parameter P, which leaves room to narrow the payload side later without touching the name side.

assistant.body: I did. P can only come from the literal, so even with K already pinned the constraint gets checked after the fact. Dropping back to K alone and taking the payload as Events[K] directly.

turns.user: good. now i also want onSave style names generated from the type. and handlers sometimes return a promise, i need to await the result

assistant.body: Rebuilding the keys with an as clause on the mapped type and a template literal for the on prefix. The result goes through a conditional type that infers the return and runs it past Awaited, so sync handlers pass through untouched.

export type Settled<H> = H extends (payload: never) => infer R ? Awaited<R> : never

export type SaveResult = Settled<Listeners['onSave']>
